label: TMUA 2017 · Paper 2 · Question 10

hints.title: Look for cancellation across the interval
hints.body: Split the integration interval at its midpoint. For the integral to cancel by symmetry, compare heights at equal distances to either side.
hints.recap: Equal and opposite heights over matching intervals cancel in a signed integral.
hints.pitfall: A zero at one or two isolated points tells you little about the whole area.
hints.pause: Write the two x-values that are equally far from the midpoint.

recall.reminder: Equal and opposite heights over matching intervals cancel in a signed integral.

hints.title: Check what each identity pairs
hints.body: For each identity involving two inputs to f, calculate the midpoint of those inputs. Check whether it pairs the interval you are integrating over.
hints.recap: The centre of the symmetry must match the interval.
hints.pitfall: A symmetry about a different point need not make this integral zero.
hints.pause: Prove the matching condition gives cancellation; use a simple function to test the others.

recall.reminder: A whole-function counterexample must satisfy the stated condition throughout its domain.

solution:
Condition D says f(2+x)=−f(2−x). For 0≤x≤1, these are opposite heights at points equally far from 2. Each contribution on [1, 2] cancels its matching contribution on [2, 3], so the total integral is 0.

The other conditions do not suffice: A allows f(x)=(x−2)2; B allows f(x)=(x−1)(x−3), whose integral is negative. C and E describe oddness about 0, and f(x)=x satisfies them but integrates to 4 on [1, 3].

D is sufficient.
knowledgePattern: Use antisymmetry about the integration midpoint as a sufficient condition
